title: Mission: Impossible, Ghost Protocol
tagline: No backup, no extraction, no leftovers.
about: When a bombing at the Kremlin is pinned on the IMF, Ethan and a small cut-off team chase a nuclear extremist from Moscow to Dubai to Mumbai.

    StartersMoscow cabbage pirozhkiSoft baked buns filled with buttery cabbage, onion, egg and dillHow to make it500g plain flour7g dried yeast1 tbsp caster sugar1 1/2 tsp salt250ml milk, warmed60g butter, melted, for the dough1 egg, for the dough2 eggs, for the filling500g white cabbage, finely shredded1 onion, diced40g butter, for the filling1/2 tsp black pepper2 tbsp dill, chopped1 egg, beaten, for brushingMix the flour, yeast, sugar and 1 tsp of the salt with the warm milk, melted butter and egg for the dough, and knead until smooth.Cover and prove until doubled. Meanwhile boil the eggs for the filling for 9 minutes, and cook the cabbage and onion slowly in the butter until soft and sweet.Season the cabbage with the rest of the salt and the pepper, cool a little, then mix in the chopped eggs and dill.Divide the dough into 16, flatten each piece, fill, pinch closed and set seam side down on lined trays.Rest the buns while the oven heats to 200°C.Brush with the beaten egg and bake until golden.Brij Nath's party onion bhajisCrisp spiced onion fritters in chickpea batter with mint and coriander yoghurtHow to make it3 onions, thinly sliced1 tsp salt150g chickpea flour2 tbsp rice flour1 tsp ground cumin1 tsp ground turmeric1 tsp chilli powder1 green chilli, finely chopped1/2 cup coriander, chopped, for the bhajis100ml water200g Greek yoghurt1/2 cup mint leaves1/2 cup coriander leaves, for the dip1 lime, juiced1 L vegetable oil, for fryingToss the onions with the salt and leave to soften.Stir in the chickpea flour, rice flour, cumin, turmeric, chilli powder, green chilli and coriander, then add the water to make a thick, sticky batter.Blend the yoghurt with the mint, coriander for the dip and lime juice.Heat the oil to 175°C in a deep pan.Fry heaped spoonfuls of batter in batches until deep golden and crisp.Drain and serve hot with the yoghurt.MainsDubai lamb machboosEmirati spiced rice with slow-cooked lamb, dried lime, cardamom and tomato, topped with fried onion, sultanas and almondsHow to make it400g basmati rice1kg boneless lamb shoulder, in 5cm pieces3 tbsp vegetable oil3 onions, sliced, one kept for the topping4 garlic cloves, crushed1 tbsp ginger, grated2 tsp ground cumin2 tsp ground coriander1 tsp ground turmeric1 cinnamon stick6 cardamom pods, cracked2 dried limes, pierced2 tomatoes, chopped1 tbsp tomato paste1 1/2 tsp salt1.5 L water50g slivered almonds50g sultanas1/2 cup coriander leavesRinse the rice and leave it to soak.Brown the lamb in batches in 2 tbsp of the oil.Add two of the onions and cook until soft.Stir in the garlic, ginger, spices, dried limes, tomatoes, tomato paste and salt.Add the water, cover and simmer until the lamb is tender.Lift out the lamb and keep warm. Measure 750ml of the broth back into the pot, add the drained rice, cover and cook on low.Rest the rice off the heat. Meanwhile fry the last onion in the rest of the oil until deep brown, adding the almonds and sultanas at the end.Pile the rice on a platter and top with the lamb, onions, almonds, sultanas and coriander.Benji's Kremlin mushroom stroganoffBenji and Ethan walking into the Kremlin behind a fake hallway screenHow to make it800g mixed mushrooms40g butter1 brown onion2 garlic cloves2 tsp sweet paprika1 tbsp plain flour250ml vegetable stock1 tsp Dijon mustard200g sour cream400g egg noodles1 dill100g dill picklesBrown the sliced mushrooms in half the butter in batches and lift out.Fry the sliced onion and garlic in the rest of the butter for 5 minutes, then stir in the paprika and flour.Add the stock and mustard, put the mushrooms back and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the sour cream off the heat.Cook the noodles, drain and toss with a little butter.Serve over the noodles with dill and pickles on the side.SweetsDubai sandstorm luqaimatCrisp cardamom and saffron dumplings tossed in warm date syrup and toasted sesameHow to make it1/4 tsp saffron threads2 tbsp milk, warmed250g plain flour1 tbsp cornflour7g dried yeast1 tbsp caster sugar1/2 tsp ground cardamom1/4 tsp salt300ml warm water1 L vegetable oil, for frying125ml date syrup1 tbsp sesame seeds, toastedSoak the saffron in the warm milk.Whisk the flour, cornflour, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt with the saffron milk and warm water into a thick, smooth batter.Cover and leave until bubbly and doubled.Heat the oil to 175°C in a deep pan.Drop in small spoonfuls of batter in batches and fry, turning, until deep golden.Drain, toss with the warmed date syrup and scatter with sesame seeds.DrinksMumbai party mango gin coolerGin shaken with fresh mango, lime and cardamom syrup, topped with soda over iceHow to make it60g caster sugar60ml water4 cardamom pods, crushed1 large mango, flesh only240ml gin2 limes, juiced2 cups ice400ml soda water, chilled1 lime, cut into wheelsSimmer the sugar, water and cardamom until dissolved, then cool and strain.Blend the mango until smooth.Shake the gin, mango, lime juice and syrup hard with ice, in two batches.Strain into four tall glasses of ice, top with soda and garnish with lime wheels.
